criteria.evidence: All five sections plus Sources and Agent intent (ICE) are substantive: e.g. Inputs / Outputs names 'the spine — each domain's `id` and `intents`, and each capability's `domain`' and 'Out: for a domain id, the list of business intents that touch it and the capabilities in it ... each with its page link'; Out of scope names the owner of each excluded concern ('/discover-domains owns that', 'fn-724 owns it', 'fn-725 owns those', 'View plans (cap-719)').

'The link is kept on both sides: when an intent's Touches list names a domain, that domain's spine `intents` names the intent, and the other way round. A play that writes one side writes the other.' and 'Out: an error from the check when a plan file has a node of kind domain, or a domain is linked to a tracker issue.'
criteria.fix: In Rules & behavior, give the two-sided rule its why and its consequence: say why both sides are kept (e.g. so a search from either the intent or the domain returns the same answer) and state whether a one-sided link found by the check is a warning for alignment or an error (the acceptance criterion only says 'reports'), in line with the capability's 'nothing is blocked' rule. Also add a rule saying how the check detects 'a domain linked to a tracker issue' (what it reads — issue labels, types, or titles — and what it reports), and add a matching Given/When/Then, since today only the plan-file case has one.

criteria.evidence: Every section is a list of discrete bullets; What it does states the function's behaviour ('A domain lists the business intents and capabilities in it, so "which business intents serve the commerce domain?" can be answered'), with no user story; all five acceptance criteria use Given/When/Then, e.g. 'Given a plan file with a node whose kind is domain, when the check runs, then it fails with an error naming the plan and the node.'

Parent says only 'In: the loose links from a domain to its business intents and capabilities, so a search by domain can be answered.' The child adds the concrete fields read (spine `intents`, capability `domain`, intent Touches list marked 'adds, changes or removes'), the output shape, edge cases ('A domain that no capability names and no intent touches is still a valid domain; the search returns it with empty lists', 'reports it as "not in the spine"', 'domains: []' case) and testable criteria.

What: 'for a domain id, the list of business intents that touch it and the capabilities in it'. Why: 'A domain is a big area of the product, kept in the model only for finding things' and 'domains set which areas the product covers, not what work is done'. Edges: 'never a level of a plan tree, never a tracker issue, and never carries an ICE', 'adding or changing a domain never changes whether anything is ready', plus named owners in Out of scope.
